pages.text: Seal the room, then insulate the floor, walls and roof.$(br2)Sealing holds air. Insulation holds heat. A glass wall does the first, not the second.

pages.title: Materials
pages.text: $(bold)Good$(): wool, snow blocks, moss$(br)$(bold)Fair$(): wood, better than stone$(br)$(bold)Poor$(): glass, metal, ice$(br2)For windows, use $(l:heating/insulated_glass)Insulated Glass$(/l).

pages.name: Layered Wall
pages.text: Room floor in front. Three layers outward, all counted.

pages.title: Layers
pages.text: Up to $(bold)three layers$() outward from each boundary add together. Layer the floor and roof too.$(br2)Thin windows can dominate your losses.

pages.title: Size
pages.text: Small rooms heat fast; large or heavy ones slowly.$(br2)Insulation saves fuel. It makes no heat.$(br2)$(flavor)Fewer windows than an aquarium, please.$()

pages.title: Depth
pages.text: The surface chills first. Below the fixed $(bold)Y 64$() reference the cold arrives late, later the deeper you go.$(br2)Above it, surface and altitude rules apply.
Deep ground is a real refuge; its warmth depends on progression and preset.$(br2)$(danger)It holds no air.$() Late Phase 6 needs EVA or a sealed room with oxygen.
